title: Gradient descent and the learning rate

0.01.behaviour: converges, but slowly — needs far more than 60 steps

1.05.behaviour: diverges — each step overshoots by more than it corrects, so the loss grows

lesson: The learning rate is the whole story on a convex surface. At 0.01 the trajectory crawls; at 0.1–0.5 it converges cleanly; at 1.05 each step overshoots by more than it corrects and the loss diverges to infinity. The threshold is not arbitrary — for a quadratic loss, gradient descent diverges once the learning rate exceeds 2/λ_max, where λ_max is the largest eigenvalue of the Hessian. That is why the same learning rate can be fine on one problem and catastrophic on another: it depends on the curvature, not on the number.

quiz.question: Why does a learning rate of 1.05 diverge here?
options: Each step overshoots by more than it corrects, so the error grows
quiz.explanation: The surface is convex with a single minimum. Divergence happens when the step size exceeds 2/λ_max: the update jumps past the minimum to a point of higher loss, and the next gradient is larger still.
